correctness.rationale: For all real 19<r<21, the proof excludes two A chores in one bundle by comparing EFX removal thresholds with the other bundles and the impossible small-chore integer equation x+7y=20. It forces the unique A-free agent to hold at least three B and three C chores and then uses a leftover-item pigeonhole contradiction. For all other r>7, seven explicit allocations have exact affine EFX feasibility intervals (7,13], [11,19], [21,23], [23,25], [25,38], [32,39], [39,infinity). Their union covers exactly the existence region. The replayed standalone standard-library checker independently recalculates all agent-pair EFX inequalities with rational arithmetic and exhaustively checks 62,720 count allocations at each of r=39/2,20,41/2. Sampling is not the universal nonexistence proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 first additive-chore EFX nonexistence construction depends on the numerical cost triple (1,7,20). Whether failure is stable under perturbation and whether arbitrarily larger large-chore costs still obstruct EFX is a structural, source-motivated gap. The exact answer has a sharp bounded failure window (19,21), restoration at both 19 and 21, and seven explicit allocations covering the exterior. Its nonmonotonic feasibility phase distinguishes robust impossibility from a single tuned example, without claiming universal results for all tri-valued instances.
